hook: Doctors want hospitals to pool data on what Hyderabad's *AQI 300* days do to us
hook_b: Doctors want hospitals to pool data on what Hyderabad's *AQI 300* days do to us
tldr: At Cyberabad Moves, doctors from KIMS, AIG and PHFI called for hospitals to share anonymised data on pollution-linked illness.

beats.what: KIMS's Dr Sudheer Vinnamala proposed hospitals share anonymised data on respiratory illness, strokes and heart conditions with health authorities.
beats.why: Hyderabad's AQI crossed 300 on Deepavali, and PM2.5 and PM10 were several times above limits, the panel heard.
beats.care: AIG pulmonologist Dr Vishwanath Gella said asthma and lung cases rise during poor-air periods, especially around Deepavali and in winter.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Doctors said daily AQI alerts could warn asthma patients, and hospitals could stagger appointments and run Metro last-mile links.

cards.q: Should hospitals share anonymised pollution-illness data with the city?

qs: What would a city health database measure first?
Which roads around schools see the most exposure?

facts.t: About *80%* of children live within 2-3 km of their schools, PHFI research shows.

viz.l: Children living within 2-3 km of school
viz.verdict: Most school trips are short, so road fixes near schools reach most kids.

watch: Whether health authorities take up the hospital data-sharing idea before the winter pollution peak.
